clinician.final_diagnosis: cutaneous melanocytic tumor with CRTC1::TRIM11 fusion
clinician.trajectory_summary: An 18-year-old female presented with a three-year history of a slow-growing, dull red, occasionally tender mass on her left leg. Initial B-ultrasound revealed a hypoechoic nodule in the proximal left leg subcutaneous soft tissue without significant lymphadenopathy. Tissue sampling demonstrated a well-circumscribed dermal nodular mass composed of epithelioid cells arranged in nests and fascicles with prominent nucleoli, visible mitosis, and local nevus cell clusters; basal margins were positive. Immunohistochemistry confirmed melanocytic differentiation with positivity for S-100, SOX10, and MelanA, focal positivity for HMB45, retained INI1 and H3K27Me3 expression, and a Ki-67 proliferation index of approximately 10%. Molecular characterization identified a CRTC1::TRIM11 fusion by next-generation sequencing, confirmed by CRTC1 FISH showing positive fracture rearrangement. The patient underwent surgical management (implied by postoperative status), and at six-month follow-up demonstrated no local recurrence or metastasis.

key_supporting_evidence.claim: Clinical presentation of slow-growing dull red mass on left leg for three years with occasional tenderness
Ultrasound demonstrated hypoechoic nodule in proximal left leg subcutaneous soft tissue without significant lymphadenopathy

Histopathology revealed well-circumscribed dermal nodular mass composed of epithelioid cells in nests/fascicles with round/oval nuclei, abundant cytoplasm, prominent nucleoli, visible mitosis, and local nevus cell clusters with positive basal margins
Immunohistochemistry positive for melanocytic markers S-100, SOX10, and MelanA; focally positive for HMB45; retained INI1 and H3K27Me3 nuclear expression; Ki-67 proliferation index approximately 10%
Molecular testing detected CRTC1::TRIM11 fusion by NGS and confirmed positive fracture rearrangement by CRTC1 FISH
Six-month postoperative follow-up showed no local recurrence or metastasis

ruled_out_or_less_likely_alternatives.basis: Retained INI1 and H3K27Me3 nuclear expression argues against MPNST (which typically shows loss of these markers)

While immunophenotype overlaps, the presence of CRTC1::TRIM11 fusion is a distinctive molecular alteration not seen in conventional melanoma, supporting classification as a specific melanocytic tumor entity
S100 negativity is typical for cellular neurothekeoma, whereas this case showed strong S100 positivity

Staging imaging studies (CT, MRI, or PET) to evaluate regional lymph nodes or distant metastasis at the time of diagnosis are not reported
Long-term follow-up beyond six months is not documented
